items.selection_reason: Proof explicitly composes two commutative squares (τ with i_* and τ with p_!) to obtain the square for f=p∘i.
concrete_content_or_checks: Square for τ/i_* over X→P^n×Y; square for τ/p_! over P^n×Y→Y; paste to τ_Yf_!=f_*τ_X.
correctness_checks: Verify domains/codomains and that pasting agrees with f=p∘i.

source_lines.91: 2.1 Composition of the two squares. Consider the two commutative squares: $\tau\circ i_*=i_*\circ\tau$ on $X\to\mathbb P^n\times_kY$ by [L1], and $\tau\circ p_!=p_*\circ\tau$ on $\mathbb P^n\times_kY\to Y$ by [L2]. Composing them gives $\tau_Y\circ p_!\circ i_!=p_*\circ i_*\circ\tau_X$, and by the functoriality of both pushforwards, $p_!\circ i_!=f_!$ and $p_*i_*=f_*$, this is exactly $\tau_Y\circ f_!=f_*\circ\tau_X$, the displayed formula. [L1, L2, L3, step 1.1, algebra]
